(`_add_argument_dests`, the `add_subparsers` dest handler)". Those line numbers map exactly onto the current file. This task's title, `origin_prompt`, and Gap prose all say **`set_defaults`** — a transcription error for `add_subparsers`.
4. **A THIRD splat-blind site exists, missed by the reviewer's own sweep.** `set_defaults` at `:197` is `defined |= {kw.arg for kw in node.keywords if kw.arg is not None}` — the `is not None` filter drops splats, so `ap.set_defaults(**DEFAULTS)` contributes NOTHING to the DEFINED set. Every attribute defined only through that splat is a false positive. `set_defaults(**SHARED)` is a more common real-world idiom than either cited site, so the body's mistaken title accidentally names a genuine third site. All three walkers are splat-blind: `:110` (`kw.arg != "dest"` -> continue), `:191` (`kw.arg == "dest"` -> never true), `:197` (`is not None`).
5. **The one-line fix sketch mechanically covers only site 1.** `dynamic_dest = True` -> `_permissive_dests(opts)` works for `_add_argument_dests`. `add_subparsers` and `set_defaults` have no `opts` list, no `dynamic_dest` flag, and no option strings to be permissive over — so "both sibling sites take the same change" is not implementable as written. This is a real design fork, not a typo.
6. **Test baseline confirmed: 17 tests, zero existing splat coverage.** Acceptance criterion 3's count is exact. Note `test_set_defaults_kwargs_define_attrs` uses an explicit `ap.set_defaults(verbose=True)` — its `**kw` docstring is signature notation, not a splat — so splat handling is genuinely untested at all three sites.
7. **Pin template identified.** `test_dynamic_dest_kwarg_takes_permissive_fallback` (R3.1) uses `add_argument("-n", "--dry-run", dest=DEST_NAME)` and asserts `args.n` is not flagged — 2 option strings so exact vs permissive derivation differ. This satisfies acceptance criterion 2 and matches the reviewer's own suggested pin (`ap.add_argument("-n", "--dry-run", **extra)` + `args.n` -> no SystemExit). A single-option fixture cannot discriminate the two implementations (the body is right to forbid it).

**Scope = all THREE splat-blind keyword walkers**, as the union of the body's stated intent (`add_argument` + `set_defaults`) and its line numbers (`add_argument` + `add_subparsers`). Fixing only the two cited sites would leave the site the title names; fixing only the title's two would leave the site the line numbers name. `Assumption:` the finding's principle — "a splat is strictly LESS resolvable, so it must not be handled MORE strictly" — is site-independent, so it binds every walker.
